brand.name: htmx
brand.what_they_do: htmx gives plain HTML access to AJAX, CSS transitions, WebSockets and server-sent events through attributes, as a small dependency-free library.
brand.audience: Web developers who want modern interfaces built with hypermedia rather than a heavy front-end framework.
brand.tone: Confident and direct, with a playful, retro-web streak (the page's haiku, its novelty ads and its uwu shirts).

type_pairing.heading: Righteous
type_pairing.why: Righteous has the chunky retro-web character the vibe asks for; Nunito is rounded and readable at small sizes, so it balances the heading.

voice: Confident and direct: it states what htmx does in short, plain sentences, as in 'high power tools for HTML'.
Playful and a little irreverent: the haiku and novelty ads make room for humor without losing the technical point.
Plain-spoken for developers: it names the real mechanisms (AJAX, WebSockets, SSE) and avoids hype.
do: Use the blue primary and cream background together for the main layout, with the orange and pink accents sparingly.
Keep the logos on a plain background with clear space around them.
Set headings in Righteous and body text in Nunito.
Keep copy short and concrete, spelling out technical terms once.
dont: Don't recolor the logos outside this palette.
Don't put the wordmark in a scene or next to other marks.
Don't use Righteous for body text or long paragraphs.
Don't claim features htmx does not have, or describe it as a framework.
